title: Policy-Based Bayesian Active Causal Discovery with Deep Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: Causal discovery requires selecting informative interventions, but intervention experiments can be costly and risky.

gap.claim: Existing Bayesian active-learning methods may select interventions myopically, causing local optimality, and may require too much time for adaptive experiments with strict inference-speed requirements.

contributions.claim: The study proposes RL-CBED, a reinforcement-learning-based causal Bayesian experimental design method intended to reduce local optimality risk and accelerate intervention-selection inference.
The active causal discovery problem is formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process, with an information-gain-based sparse reward improved into a dense reward.
The study theoretically establishes that the Q-function estimator can be learned using trajectories sampled only from the prior.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe RL-CBED as a novel method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world-inspired semi-synthetic datasets.
The authors report that these experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

narrative_sequence.summary: Causal discovery using observational and interventional data is important, while intervention selection is constrained by cost and risk.
Bayesian active learning selects interventions by expected information gain, but existing approaches face local-optimality and time-cost limitations.
RL-CBED formulates active causal discovery as a POMDP and uses progressively refined reward design to support faster policy learning.
The Q-function estimator can be learned from trajectories sampled from the prior.
Experiments on synthetic and real-world-inspired semi-synthetic datasets are reported as demonstrating effectiveness.
